items.stem: Under the Gentleman’s Agreement of 1907-08, how was Japanese labour immigration limited?
items.stemEs: Según el Gentleman’s Agreement de 1907-08, ¿cómo se limitó la inmigración laboral japonesa?

choices.text: Congress excluded Japanese labourers by statute, as it had Chinese labourers
choices.textEs: El Congreso excluyó por ley a los trabajadores japoneses, como había hecho con los chinos
choices.explanation: Congress did eventually exclude Japanese immigration by statute — in the Immigration Act of 1924, sixteen years later. In 1907 the point of the arrangement was to avoid exactly that kind of law.
choices.misconception: merges the negotiated arrangement with the exclusion statute that came much later

choices.text: Japan agreed to stop issuing passports to departing labourers
choices.textEs: Japón acordó dejar de expedir pasaportes a los trabajadores que emigraban

choices.text: A literacy test screened out labourers who could not read
choices.textEs: Una prueba de alfabetización excluía a los trabajadores que no sabían leer
choices.explanation: The literacy test was a real nativist instrument, proposed for decades and finally enacted over a veto in 1917. It was aimed at European arrivals and formed no part of this arrangement.
choices.misconception: substitutes the literacy test for the passport mechanism this arrangement used

choices.text: San Francisco agreed to end the segregation of Japanese schoolchildren
choices.textEs: San Francisco acordó poner fin a la segregación de los escolares japoneses
choices.explanation: True, and it is the other half of the bargain: the United States gave this in return. The question asks how labour immigration was limited, and a school board's reversal does not limit it.
choices.misconception: answers with what the United States conceded rather than how immigration was limited

items.dokRationale: The student retrieves the mechanism the arrangement used. No relationship has to be reasoned out, so recognising the passport restriction is recall.
items.explanation: The arrangement was informal and never went to the Senate, which is what distinguished it from a statute. Japan undertook to withhold passports from labourers, so the restriction was applied at the point of departure by Japan's own government rather than imposed on Japan by American law.
items.explanationEs: El acuerdo fue informal y nunca pasó por el Senado, lo que lo distinguía de una ley. Japón se comprometió a negar pasaportes a los trabajadores, de modo que la restricción se aplicaba en el punto de salida por el propio gobierno japonés y no se le imponía a Japón mediante una ley estadounidense.

items.stem: Why did the United States handle Japanese immigration through the Gentleman’s Agreement rather than a law like the Chinese Exclusion Act?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué Estados Unidos abordó la inmigración japonesa mediante el Gentleman’s Agreement en lugar de una ley como la Ley de Exclusión China?

choices.text: Japanese arrivals were fewer than Chinese arrivals had been
choices.textEs: Las llegadas japonesas eran menos numerosas que las chinas
choices.explanation: That is true, and it is not the reason. Numbers had not stopped Congress before, and the agitation in California was fierce whatever the totals; what differed was who would have to be insulted.
choices.misconception: offers a true comparison of numbers as the reason for the different method

choices.text: The Supreme Court had struck down the Chinese Exclusion Act in 1889
choices.textEs: La Corte Suprema había anulado la Ley de Exclusión China en 1889
choices.explanation: The Court did rule on exclusion in 1889, and it UPHELD the law, holding that excluding foreigners was an attribute of sovereignty. The decision pointed the opposite way from this option.
choices.misconception: reverses the outcome of the Court's 1889 ruling on exclusion

choices.text: Japan was a rising power and would have taken offence at a statute
choices.textEs: Japón era una potencia en ascenso y se habría ofendido ante una ley de exclusión

choices.text: Congress had already barred all Asian immigration in the 1882 Act
choices.textEs: El Congreso ya había prohibido toda la inmigración asiática en la ley de 1882
choices.explanation: The 1882 Act reached Chinese labourers, not all Asians, and it left merchants, students and diplomats outside its terms. Reading it as a general Asian exclusion overstates what it did.
choices.misconception: widens a law aimed at Chinese labourers into a bar on all Asian immigration

items.dokRationale: The student has to connect a country's international standing to the form a restriction took. Naming the arrangement would be recall; explaining why the method differed is a relationship.
items.explanation: China in 1882 had no leverage to object to being named in an American statute. Japan by 1907 had defeated Russia at sea, and Roosevelt wanted its goodwill, so the restriction was arranged as a face-saving undertaking by Japan itself rather than written into law over its protest.
items.explanationEs: China, en 1882, no tenía capacidad para oponerse a ser nombrada en una ley estadounidense. Japón, hacia 1907, había derrotado a Rusia en el mar y Roosevelt quería su buena voluntad, por lo que la restricción se dispuso como un compromiso voluntario de Japón que salvaba las apariencias, en lugar de imponerse por ley contra su protesta.

items.stem: After the Chinese Exclusion Act, what was the main legislative instrument nativists used against European immigration before 1917?
items.stemEs: Después de la Ley de Exclusión China, ¿cuál fue el principal instrumento legislativo que los nativistas usaron contra la inmigración europea antes de 1917?

choices.text: A national-origins quota system enacted in the 1890s
choices.textEs: Un sistema de cuotas por origen nacional aprobado en la década de 1890
choices.explanation: National-origins quotas were real and decisive, and they arrived in 1921 and 1924 — a generation after the 1890s. Before the First World War no quota system existed.
choices.misconception: moves the quota system back three decades from the 1920s to the 1890s

choices.text: The American Protective Association's campaign against Catholic officeholders
choices.textEs: La campaña de la American Protective Association contra funcionarios católicos
choices.explanation: The Association was real, founded in 1887, and anti-Catholic agitation was a genuine part of this nativism. It worked through elections and pressure rather than legislation, and the question asks for the legislative instrument.
choices.misconception: answers with a political campaign rather than with a legislative instrument

choices.text: State laws barring immigrants from owning farmland
choices.textEs: Leyes estatales que prohibían a los inmigrantes poseer tierras de cultivo
choices.explanation: Alien land laws were real — California passed one in 1913 — but they were aimed at Japanese farmers on the Pacific coast, not at European arrivals, and they were state rather than federal.
choices.misconception: applies laws written against Asian landholding to European immigration

choices.text: Proposals for a literacy test three presidents vetoed before 1917
choices.textEs: Propuestas de una prueba de alfabetización que tres presidentes vetaron antes de 1917

items.dokRationale: The student has to sort real nativist activity by kind — legislative against political — and then place it correctly in time. Naming nativism would be recall; identifying its legislative vehicle requires both distinctions.
items.explanation: A reading requirement would have fallen hardest on the southern and eastern Europeans the restrictionists wanted to keep out, while sounding like a test of merit rather than of origin. Cleveland, Taft and Wilson each vetoed it; Congress finally overrode Wilson in 1917.
items.explanationEs: Un requisito de lectura habría afectado sobre todo a los europeos del sur y del este a quienes los restriccionistas querían excluir, aunque sonara como una prueba de mérito y no de origen. Cleveland, Taft y Wilson lo vetaron cada uno; el Congreso finalmente anuló el veto de Wilson en 1917.
